item.title: Centroids Of Partially Commutative Two-step Nilpotent Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we describe the centroid (according to S. Lioutikov and A. Myasnikov) of an arbitrary finitely generated graph two-step nilpotent Hall exponential group over a binomial domain whose commutativity graph has no central vertices. Based on this description, we prove that if the non-commutativity graph of such a group has exactly one connected component and the group is non-Abelian, then the group is rigid.
item.dc:creator: Ivan M. Buchinskiy

item.title: On the factorization graph of finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.40860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a finite group $G$, the factorization graph $\Gamma(G)$ has as vertices the nontrivial proper subgroups of $G$, with two distinct vertices $H$ and $K$ adjacent if and only if $HK = G$. In this paper, we study structural and combinatorial properties of $\Gamma(G)$ for three families of groups: cyclic groups of square-free order, generalized quaternion groups, and dicyclic groups. For cyclic groups $C_{p_1\cdots p_r}$, we describe the global structure of $\Gamma(G)$ and determine its order, degree sequence, center, girth, and diameter. We also characterize completely when $\Gamma(G)$ is claw-free, show that it is non-planar for $r \geq 4$, and prove that after removing all pendant vertices, the resulting induced subgraph is 2-connected; we further compute its exact circumference for small $r$, showing it is Hamiltonian precisely when $r=4, 5$. For generalized quaternion groups, we classify all isolated vertices and prove that the reduced factorization graph has diameter two and a unique central vertex. Moreover, we show that it is planar, has chromatic number~$3$, is Eulerian, and non-Hamiltonian, and that it contains maximal induced stars and triangular book subgraphs. Finally, we analyze the dicyclic case and show that the reduced factorization graph is a complete bipartite graph, from which all main invariants follow directly. An explicit SageMath algorithm for constructing $\Gamma(G)$ is included.
item.dc:creator: Ismael Guti\'errez, Yesneri Zuleta y E. J. Garc\'ia-Claro

item.title: Short Jennings series and the modular isomorphism problem
item.description:
arXiv:2610.40868v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $p$ be an odd prime and $G$ a finite $p$-group whose Jennings series has length at most $p$, that is, $D_{p+1}(G)=1$; when $D_p(G)
e1$ assume also that $G/D_p(G)$ has nilpotency class at most $p-2$. We prove that $G$ is determined up to isomorphism by its modular group algebra $\mathbb{F}_p G$, and indeed by the quotient $\mathbb{F}_p G/\mathrm{I}^{\,
u+1}$, where $\mathrm{I}$ is the augmentation ideal and $
u$ the length of the Jennings series; for an arbitrary finite $p$-group $G$, the quotient $\mathbb{F}_p G/\mathrm{I}^{\,p}$ determines $G/D_p(G)$; and that every automorphism of $\mathbb{F}_p G$ is the product of an automorphism of $G$ and an automorphism inducing the identity on $\mathrm{I}/\mathrm{I}^2$. In particular the modular isomorphism problem has a positive answer for all $p$-groups of exponent $p$ and class less than $p$, and for all $p$-groups of class at most $p-2$ and exponent dividing $p^2$ whose derived subgroup has exponent $p$. Consequently every counterexample in odd characteristic has class at least $p-1$, or a derived subgroup of exponent at least $p^2$, or an element of order $p^3$. The proof combines a descent theorem in the truncated group algebra of a free group, valid for every prime, with a relative rigidity theorem for the unipotent automorphisms of truncated group algebras of groups of exponent $p$, proved through the Lazard correspondence. The bound $p$ is the range in which the logarithm of the group algebra exists.
item.dc:creator: Diego Tuzzolo

item.title: Functorial Analysis of Group-Alphabet Cellular Automata
item.description: arXiv:2610.41013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G$ be a group and let $n\in\mathbb N$. We consider one-dimensional cellular automata of length $n$ over the alphabet $G$, with periodic boundary conditions and with local rules $\phi$ given by words. We construct a functor $F$ from $\mathbf{Grp}$, the category of groups (or any similar algebraic structure), to the category of pointed digraphs, and show its faithfulness. We introduce the image category $\mathcal C_{n,\phi}$ of state transition graphs of all such group-alphabet cellular automata, and show $F$ is an equivalence onto this category. Consequently we investigate the translation of categorical structures in $\mathbf{Grp}$ in terms of automata, and give examples of how standard methods of homological algebra may now be applied to automata. Additionally, a graph-theoretical construction of the product in $\mathcal C_{n,\phi}$ is given, together with a formula for cycle lengths and multiplicities in this product. When $G$ is abelian, further structural properties of state transition graphs follow, and we contrast these results with non-abelian counterexamples.
item.dc:creator: Fran\c{c}ois Huard, Nathan Dion Larivi\`ere

item.title: A local-to-global fixed point theorem for $\CAT(0)$ spaces with a uniform elliptic gap
item.description: arXiv:2610.41468v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A finitely generated group acting locally elliptically on a complete \CAT(0) space of finite geometric dimension fixes a point if distances to elliptic fixed sets are uniformly controlled by displacements. For arbitrary groups, the same hypothesis gives a fixed point in the space or its visual boundary. The proof combines a first-moment random-walk displacement estimate with Izeki's zero-drift theorem. For finite-rank $\R$-buildings whose Euclidean metric factor has finite linear image, we obtain an all-type local-to-global theorem, including the nondiscrete $\widetilde G_2$ case, with an explicit gap and without metric completeness; the linear-image restriction can be removed from the fixed-point conclusion when the Euclidean factor has dimension at most three. A tangent-cone criterion characterizes the gap and yields a cubical bound with optimal asymptotic growth $d/\pi$ in dimension $d$. For Hadamard manifolds, the gap is equivalent to uniformly bounded finite stabilizers in the isometry image, with stabilizer bounds of optimal polynomial growth in the gap constant.
item.dc:creator: Jeroen Schillewaert

item.title: On finite simple groups possessing a conjugacy class of size 3p^n
item.description: arXiv:2610.41488v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify all non-abelian finite simple groups that possess conjugacy classes of size $3p^n$ for some prime $p$ and non-negative integer $n$. As an application, we study the structure of the normal closure $\langle g^G\rangle$ of an element $g$ in an arbitrary finite group $G$, provided that the conjugacy class $g^G$ has size $3p^n$. Specifically, we provide conditions for $\langle g^{G}\rangle$ to be solvable and completely determine its quotient modulo the solvable radical in the non-solvable case.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Beltr\'an, Changguo Shao

item.title: Hopficity of braided and labeled Thompson groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.42050v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the braided Thompson groups $BV$ and $BF$ are Hopfian, answering the two parts of Zaremsky's question. We also prove that, for every discrete group $G$, the labeled Thompson group $V(G)$ is Hopfian if and only if $G$ is Hopfian, proving a conjecture of Wu--Wu--Zhao--Zhou. The second result allows us to prove a new embedding result for Hopfian groups: every Hopfian group of type $F_n$ embeds quasi-isometrically as a subgroup of a Hopfian, boundedly acyclic, acyclic group of type $F_n$ that has no proper finite-index subgroups.
item.dc:creator: Mengfei Zhao

item.title: Non-sofic Tarski monsters
item.description: arXiv:2610.42140v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the existence of non-sofic Tarski monsters of every sufficiently large prime exponent and of torsion-free non-sofic Tarski monsters. The proof combines a theorem of Sandhu--Thom with quotient theorems of Semenov. These groups are minimal non-sofic, since all their proper subgroups are cyclic. A theorem of Minasyan--Osin--Witzel gives continuum many pairwise non-quasi-isometric torsion-free simple examples. Kulikova's quotient theorem also yields non-simple minimal non-sofic groups of exponent $p^m$ for every $m\geq2$ and every sufficiently large prime $p$. We then study descending chains of non-sofic subgroups in other constructions. We give proper self-embeddings of the binary Leavitt unit group, higher Brin--Thompson groups and the hyperbolic group studied by Douglas and Mghirbi. The explicit Kun--Thom wreath products and doubles are locally graded. These examples are $\omega$-non-sofic, and the locally graded ones contain no minimal non-sofic subgroup.
item.dc:creator: K{\i}van\c{c} Ersoy

item.title: Group Isomorphism and the Polylogarithmic-Time Hierarchy: Depth-2$\frac{1}{2}$ Circuits and Lower Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2608.26257v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the low-depth circuit complexity of Group Isomorphism in the multiplication (Cayley) table model. We prove the first circuit lower bounds for Group Isomorphism: namely, we show that every family of depth-$2$ Boolean circuits deciding Group Isomorphism requires quasipolynomial-size. (We also extend this to a limited class of depth-3 circuits, namely $\textsf{CNF}$-of-$\textsf{XOR}$s.) We complement this with upper bounds of uniform depth-$2\frac{1}{2}$ circuits of quasipolynomial-size: depth 3 circuits with poly-logarithmic bottom fan-in. A sequence of previous results from 1970-2025 progressively reduced the circuit depth from polynomial to $3\frac{1}{2}$; all of these results relied on the generator-enumerator strategy and, in fact, applied more generally to quasigroups. In contrast, our depth-$2\frac{1}{2}$ construction follows a fundamentally different strategy that exploits structure more specific to groups. We guess a composition series for each group, together with generators for its terms and the isomorphism types of its composition factors. We then inductively verify that the corresponding extensions at each level of the two composition series are compatible. A central part in this approach brings to bear the extensive work on the Short Presentation Conjecture, in tandem with the algorithmic theory of group extensions and cohomology.
item.dc:creator: Joshua A. Grochow, G\"ulce Karde\c{s}, Michael Levet

item.title: Cutoff for random Cayley graphs of finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.41347v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the random walk on a Cayley graph of a finite group whose generators are chosen independently and uniformly at random. We show that, for every finite group, the walk exhibits cutoff with high probability whenever the number of generators is large compared with the logarithm of the order of the group but small compared with every positive power of it. The cutoff time is the time at which the expected entropy of the walk comes close to its maximum, and in general it depends on the structure of the group. This settles a conjecture of Aldous and Diaconis.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Zhu

item.title: IRA Rigidity and boomerang subalgebras of group von Neumann algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.41417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the notion of Boomerang subalgebras of group von Neumann algebras and study their general properties. We show that every Boomerang subalgebra of $L(\Gamma)$ is the group von Neumann algebra of a Boomerang subgroup when $\Gamma$ is a countable $C^*$-simple acylindrically hyperbolic group or a finite product of such groups. Consequently, every such group is invariant random algebra (IRA) rigid: every IRA arises as the pushforward of an invariant random subgroup (IRS) under the group von Neumann algebra construction. We also establish IRA rigidity for adjoint $K$-split higher rank $S$-arithmetic groups, as well as for all countable mixed identity-free (MIF) groups and their finite products. Consequently, IRA rigidity holds for countable groups admitting a topologically free minimal extremely proximal action on a compact Hausdorff space with more than two points. The same conclusion holds for countable groups admitting a faithful minimal action of general type on a tree whose induced boundary action is topologically free, and for finite products of groups admitting either of these actions.
item.dc:creator: Tattwamasi Amrutam, Yair Glasner, Yair Hartman, Yongle Jiang

item.title: Infinite periodic groups of even exponents
item.description: arXiv:1810.08372v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give a new proof that free Burnside groups of sufficiently large even exponents are infinite. The method is very flexible and can also be used to study (partially) periodic quotients of any group which admits an action on a hyperbolic space satisfying a weak form of acylindricity.
item.dc:creator: R\'emi Coulon (IRMAR)

item.title: Hecke Algebra-valued Poincar\'e Series and Geometric Factorization of Affine Weyl Groups
item.description: arXiv:1903.00703v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper studies affine Weyl groups through the geometry of geodesic tubes and their hyperbolic stabilizers. We introduce a geometric framework relating affine Weyl group factorizations to Hecke-algebra-valued Poincar\'e series and zeta functions on quotient complexes. Using this framework, we prove a conjecture describing the connection between geodesic tubes and factorizations of Poincar\'e series for affine Weyl groups. We also establish partial results toward a Hecke-algebra-valued zeta identity for simply connected groups, including the cases of types $\widetilde{A}_{n-1}$ and $\widetilde{C}_n$. These results highlight the interaction between affine Weyl group geometry, Hecke algebras, and zeta functions arising from Bruhat--Tits buildings.
item.dc:creator: Ming-Hsuan Kang, Jiu Kang Yu

item.title: Small measure expansion in connected noncompact groups
item.description: arXiv:2111.05236v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Assuming $G$ is unimodular and $K>1$, and that $\mu(A^2) < K \mu(A)$. We show that this is a continuous surjective group homomorphism $\chi: G \to L$ with a compact kernel, where $L$ is a Lie group satisfying $$\dim(L) \leq \lfloor\log K\rfloor(\lfloor\log K\rfloor+1)/2.$$ This dimension bound is sharp, We also establish the relationship between $A$ and its image under the quotient map, and obtain a more general version of this result for the product set $AB$ without assuming unimodularity. We present two applications: (1) An inverse Kemperman theorem in noncompact groups. Let $G$ be a connected, noncompact, locally compact group with a left Haar measure $\mu$, and let $A$ and $B$ be nonempty, compact subsets of $G$. We classify all cases where $G$, $A$, and $B$ exhibit nearly minimal expansion properties (in the unimodular case, this means $\mu(AB)$ is close to $\mu(A) + \mu(B)$). This result completes the noncompact cases of the Kemperman inverse problem and resolves a question posed by Griesmer and Tao. (2) An effective generalized Margulis lemma for discrete subgroups of almost-connected locally compact groups acting properly by isometries. If $B(x,4r)$ can be covered by $K$ translates of $B(x,r)$ at one point and one scale, it gives a small radius $r/2M$, and the group generated at this radius has a subgroup of index at most $M \exp((\log K)^4)$ which is nilpotent modulo a finite normal subgroup. The nilpotency step is bounded by $(\log K)^2$, and \[ M\leq K^{\exp(C(\log K)^4\log\log K)} \] and $C$ is an absolute constant.
item.dc:creator: Jinpeng An, Yifan Jing, Chieu-Minh Tran, Ruixiang Zhang

item.title: Irreducible representations of tree automorphism groups into Pontryagin spaces
item.description: arXiv:2508.02367v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let G = Aut(T) be the automorphism group of a regular tree T. We study continuous irreducible representations of G that preserve a continuous strongly nondegenerate sesquilinear form of finite index on a Hilbert space. These are already classified for index 0 (unitary case) and for index 1. We show that there are no more representations for index > 1, which completes the classification.
item.dc:creator: Federico Viola

item.title: On cohomological dimensions of totally disconnected locally compact groups
item.description: arXiv:2601.12958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we introduce Mackey functors for a t.d.l.c. group and define the cohomological dimension of this group over the Mackey category. We then compare this dimension to the rational discrete cohomological dimension defined by Castellano and Weigel, as well as to the Bredon cohomological dimension of that t.d.l.c. group with respect to the family of compact open subgroups. We also extend results about the geometric dimension of a t.d.l.c. group.
item.dc:creator: Ilaria Castellano, Nadia Mazza, Brita Nucinkis

item.title: Substitution groups of formal power series
item.description: arXiv:2606.11461v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $G$ be the group of power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots\in R[[x]]$ under substitution, where $R$ is a commutative ring with $1\neq 0$ of prime characteristic $p$. Given any $n\geq 1$, the subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in R\}$ is normal in $G$, and the quotient $G_n=G/K_n$ is the group of truncated polynomials over $R$ of degree $\leq n$ under substitution. In this paper, we compute the exponent of the image of $K_r$ in $G_n$, for all $r,n\geq 1$, indicating in every case a family of elements realizing this exponent.
item.dc:creator: Agust\'in D'Alessandro, Fernando Szechtman

item.title: Strongly Primitive Salem Growth Polynomials for Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
item.description: arXiv:2606.29397v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study standard spherical growth rates of right-angled Coxeter groups through the clique polynomial of the defining graph. We prove that every even degree at least four occurs as the degree of a strongly primitive Salem growth rate: for each $d\geq2$, there are infinitely many connected $K_{2d+1}$-free defining graphs whose full reciprocal-radius polynomial is an irreducible Salem polynomial of degree $2d$. We also establish independence-polynomial obstructions for prescribed Salem polynomials, including a sharp first-coefficient bound $a_1\leq-5$. Finally, an elementary golden-ratio growth gap excludes Lehmer's number from the standard spherical growth rates of right-angled Coxeter groups.
item.dc:creator: Mingyu Oh

item.title: A cube complex for virtual Artin groups
item.description: arXiv:2607.24840v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma$ be a Coxeter graph, and let $S$ be its vertex set. An elemental complex over $\Gamma$ is an abstract simplicial complex $\mathcal D$ on $S$ that contains every pair $\{s, t\}$ with $s \neq t$ and $m_{s,t} \neq \infty$. To each elemental complex $\mathcal D$, we associate a cube complex $\Xi_{\mathcal D}$ on which the virtual Artin group ${\rm VA} [\Gamma]$ acts. We prove that $\Xi_{\mathcal D}$ is connected, simply connected, and locally regular; that the action of ${\rm VA}[\Gamma]$ on $\Xi_{\mathcal D}$ is regular, cocompact, and by isometries; and that the stabilizers of cells are parabolic subgroups. We finally prove that $\Xi_{\mathcal D}$ is CAT(0) if and only if ${\mathcal D}$ is a flag complex.
item.dc:creator: Jos\'e Galvez Mateos (IMUS), Luis Paris (IMB)

item.title: A power-commutator presentation for the group of truncated polynomials under substitution
item.description: arXiv:2610.01469v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Given a prime $p$, the Nottingham group $G(p)$ is the group of formal power series $x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3+\cdots$, $a_i\in{\bf Z}/p{\bf Z}$, under substitution. For $n\geq 1$, we write $G_n(p)$ for the quotient of $G(p)$ by its normal subgroup $K_n=\{x+a_{n+1}x^{n+1}+a_{n+2}x^{n+2}+\cdots\,|\, a_i\in {\bf Z}/p{\bf Z}\}$, namely the group of truncated polynomials $x+a_2x^2+\cdots+a_nx^n$, $a_i\in {\bf Z}/p{\bf Z}$, under substitution, which is a $p$-group of order $p^{n-1}$ generated by $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^n$. In this paper, we determine the power-commutator presentation of $G_{15}(p)$ relative to $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^{15}$. This, in turn, automatically gives the power-commutator presentation of $G_{n}(p)$ relative to $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^{n}$ for any $1\leq n<15$, as well as the initial segments of the power and commutator relations in $G_{n}(p)$ corresponding to $x+x^2,\dots,x+x^{15}$ for any $n>15$.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Szechtman

item.title: Profinite groups whose closed subgroups are subnormal of defect at most two
item.description: arXiv:2610.31878v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we classify profinite groups whose closed subgroups are subnormal of defect at most two, providing profinite versions of theorems due to Heineken and to Mahdavianary. We also establish that if G is a finitely generated periodic pro-{\pi} group, where {\pi} is a finite set of odd primes, and all its procyclic subgroups are subnormal of defect at most 2, then G is a finite {\pi}-group in which every abelian subgroup is subnormal of defect at most 2.
item.dc:creator: A. L. P. Porto, I. Lima, M. Silva

item.title: Permutation twisted cohomology, remixed
item.description: arXiv:2509.00954v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For each endotrivial complex for a $p$-group arising from Bredon homology of a representation sphere, we construct $p$-local quasi-isomorphisms, called forerunners. These enable us to extend Balmer--Gallauer's results concerning the tensor-triangular geometry of permutation modules for elementary abelian $p$-groups to all $p$-groups. We construct an open cover of the Balmer spectrum under which all endotrivials are tt-line bundles, that is, every endotrivial is locally isomorphic to a shift of the tensor unit. We define a remixed permutation twisted cohomology ring for which the canonical comparison map from the Balmer spectrum to the homogeneous spectrum of the twisted cohomology ring is injective. If the twisted cohomology ring is Noetherian, the comparison map is an open immersion, and the open cover endows the Balmer spectrum with Dirac scheme structure. We prove Noetherianity holds for Dedekind groups and the dihedral group of order 8, and conjecture it holds for all $p$-groups.
item.dc:creator: Sam K. Miller

item.title: The geometric combinatorics of $k$-shuffle braid groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.28986v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is the first in a series of two which aims at introducing a new family of groups called $k$-shuffle braid groups, denoted $\mathcal{B}_{n}(k)$. These groups have two intrinsically related stories. They were first observed by Calegari in arXiv:2105.11265 by looking at spaces of complex monic polynomials of degree $n$ whose critical values lie in $\mathbb{C} \setminus \{1, e^{\frac{2\pi i}{k}}, \dots, e^{\frac{2\pi i (k-1)}{k}}\}$. The $k$-shuffle braid groups are the fundamental groups of those spaces, which correspond geometrically to complements of $k$ translates of the discriminant variety. The second story starts from the poset of $k$-shuffle partitions, which were introduced by Drew Armstrong and explored in depth in his thesis arXiv:math/0611106. In this paper, we focus on the combinatorial aspects of $k$-shuffle braid groups starting from the poset of $k$-shuffle non-crossing partitions. We build a CW-complex on which the groups act freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly, which we show is CAT(0) for dimension up to 7. For higher dimension, we show that the CAT(0) property is implied by the conjecture of Brady and McCammond that the dual braid complex is CAT(0) (arXiv:0909.4778).
item.dc:creator: Chlo\'e Postel-Vinay
